correctness.rationale: Reconstructed source equations and hypotheses, separately verified source Theorem 5 provides almost-sure confidence limits and confidence-one endpoint agreement; the new predictable-sampling lemma is valid because receptiveness at t is F_t-measurable while U_t is an independent uniform fresh draw. Confidence-zero edges cannot have infinitely many selected positive interactions since each creates c(t+1)>=gamma; conditional Borel–Cantelli excludes infinitely many unselected flashes. Confidence-one edges are eventually receptive by c->1 and opinion-gap->0. Finite union produces an almost-surely finite global T. Endpoints gamma=1,delta=0,mu=1/2 and disconnected graphs fit the same proof. Exact-rational transition and energy checks plus deterministic examples were executed. No numerical simulation is mistaken for infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The original paper explicitly leaves a.s. eventual constancy for the same adaptive DW model unproved and proves only exclusion of edges between distinct limiting opinion clusters. The new conditional-sampling argument closes the genuine between-selection gap and handles same-cluster edges with confidence tending to zero. Baseline DW and synchronous adaptive HK constancy theorems are for different processes. A 2026 same-author edge-weighted model changes sampling weights and fixes the confidence radius; its theorem does not imply this result. Primary-literature and mathematical-record searches found no covering statement; independent exhaustive bibliographic certainty is not asserted.

value.rationale: The exact existence of a limiting effective graph for the asynchronous adaptive-confidence DW model is a specific explicitly articulated unresolved mathematical question in its foundational paper. The result settles it for arbitrary finite graphs and all nondegenerate feedback parameters and identifies the stabilized edge set through the confidence limit and infinite selected-positive interactions. It handles the structurally difficult case where the confidence-zero edge joins equal-limit opinions; it is not a routine renaming, a finite computation, or a trivial corollary of the source Theorem 6. It supplies no uniform expected stabilization time and does not overclaim consensus.
